reads.perf: The group is +4.2% versus SPY over 1M but -5.1% over 3M and -8.7% over 6M. The bounce came from large-cap guidance raises at LIN, ECL and PPG and the 10Y pulling back from 5.36%, not broad participation (51% 1M breadth).
reads.risk: Beta of 0.45, a -10.2% max drawdown and a 0.83 Sharpe reflect contracted gas cash flows at LIN and APD. Rates are the main factor at -2.0% per +25bp on the 10Y. Credit distress sits at the 98th percentile since 2024 and IG spreads are ~12bp wider, a quiet build-up of risk.
reads.fund: TTM revenue grew 4.5% and earnings 7.6%, and quarterly revenue growth re-accelerated from -2.4% (2025-Q3) to +10.6% (2026-Q2), mostly on price rather than volume (LIN volume +2%). The 10.9% operating margin and 7.2% ROIC are middling.
reads.health: D/E is 0.88, the current ratio 1.43 and interest cover 5.5x. Net debt/EBITDA is steady near 2.6x and inventory days are down to 66 (-11% y/y), so there is no destock risk. Still, 36% of cap has stretched balance sheets (ECL, APD, IFF, LYB, ESI, WLK) facing ~5.86% high-grade corporate yields.
reads.val: Trailing P/E of 43.8x is inflated by APD's $2.9B charge and LIN's $425M restructuring. Forward is 20.5x, and 14.9x ex-top-three. The NTM-earnings reverse DCF implies 1.0% growth against 7.3% consensus, and the FCF version implies 4.9% against 3.4% revenue history: in line, not stretched.
reads.earn: The beat rate is 60% with a +2.9% median EPS surprise. Guidance went up at LIN, ECL, PPG and APD, while SHW only narrowed around $12 and AXTA missed. Breadth of -0.20 and a -0.1% median 30-day revision show the headline +24% is a CLMT artifact.
reads.cycle: Cycle: late cycle, pricing power moderate. Demand across the 49-company group is price-led rather than volume-led: TTM revenue grew 4.5%, but LIN volume was only 2%, ECL guides 1-2% volume against 5-6% pricing into H1 2027, and SHW Paint Stores volume rose only low single digits.
reads.macro: MIXED: MIXED: Hormuz-driven Brent at $115.4 and a Fed that hiked to 4.00% and still prices a December hike (~78%) collide with a 43.8x P/E, while a US/Europe gas split (Henry Hub $3.06 vs TTF ~EUR93-97) and the AI capex upswing keep gases and electronics earning.

reads.perf: The cap-weighted group beat SPY by 28.8% over 1Y and 14.6% in the last month, driven by PM (+49%) and MO (+45%) as money rotated from AI tech into defensives. The median stock fell 34% and 1Y breadth is 30%, so the gains are concentrated entirely in the big three.
reads.risk: Beta of -0.19, volatility of 23.4% and a -14.3% max drawdown look defensive, but the measured -1.3% per +25bp on the 10-year shows the real risk factor is rates. The 13F put/call ratio rose to 0.94 as hedging grew, and the 1.5-sigma one-month downside is -9.1%.
reads.fund: The big three earn about 45% (PM) and 64.5% (MO smokeable OCI) margins, and pricing offsets volume declines. The -113.7% TTM earnings growth and -1.1% net margin are distortions from small-cap losses and one-offs. Industry FCF margin of 31% and ROIC of 22.4% are healthy.
reads.health: D/E of 0.71, interest cover of 6.7x and net debt/EBITDA falling to 1.36 support dividends and buybacks. The weak balance sheets sit in UVV (net debt above $1bn) and the micro-caps, which are about 0% of industry weight.
reads.val: A P/E of 21.4 at the 91st percentile and a 16.8x forward multiple are full, yet the 7.25% FCF yield implies FCF shrinking 4.1% a year. The cheap cash flow sits mostly in BTI (10.2x trailing), while PM (30.3x) prices in smoke-free success.
reads.earn: MO raised its guide to $5.66-5.74, partly on duty drawback, and PM beat its Q3 target with $2.36. BTI guided to the lower end of its ranges. Revisions are -0.7% over 30 days with breadth of -0.12, and the February guides are the real test.

reads.perf: The cap-weighted group beat SPY by 15.9% in one month and 10.9% over three, but trails by 11.5% over a year, with -4.6% annual alpha and a Sharpe of -0.04. The recent rally reflects record volumes and rotation out of AI tech; the one-year lag is COIN (-56%) and SPGI (-5%).
reads.risk: Beta of 0.44 and 23.2% vol partly reflect internal hedging: hedging volumes rise when equities fall. The hedge fails in the credit channel, the strongest measured factor at -3% per -2% in HY bonds, with the NY Fed distress index at its 99th percentile.
reads.fund: A 40.2% operating margin and 38.4% FCF margin are elite. TTM revenue growth of 4.2% and earnings growth of 1.1% are depressed by COIN's -27% revenue; large caps are growing 9-15%. Quarterly revenue growth has slowed from 21.0% y/y (2024-Q4) to 4.3% (2026-Q3), and DSO is up 3.1% y/y.

reads.val: 28.8x trailing is 16% below the five-year median of 34.2x, but the long-history P/E is at the 60th percentile since 2008 (26.4 vs a 24.8 median), where 12M returns have had a median of +3.0%.
reads.earn: An 82% beat rate with a 2.7% median EPS surprise and Q3 beats at CME, ICE, NDAQ and MSCI set up a strong Q4 for the venues, locked in by October's 30M ADV. MCO guides Q4 issuance down mid-teens, and TRU guides Q4 organic growth of 3-6%.

reads.risk: A beta of 2.31, 42.8% volatility and a -30.2% max drawdown make this a leveraged bet on the S&P 500 and on credit. A 2% high-yield selloff has meant -10.9% for the group, and +25bp on the 10-year about -2.4%.
